notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

# tpch_q10v_20.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    nation_facts = get(db, "nation/3", Relation())
    customer_facts = get(db, "customer/3", Relation())
    orders_facts = get(db, "orders/5", Relation())
    lineitem_facts = get(db, "lineitem/13", Relation())

    customer = customer_facts

    nation = nation_facts

    nation_by_1 = index(nation, 1)
    customer_nation = Relation()
    # customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
    for ((C, N, _), x1) in customer
        for ((_, Name, _), x2) in get(nation_by_1, (N,), NONE)
            add!(customer_nation, (C, Name), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    lineitem = lineitem_facts

    orders = orders_facts

    lineitem_by_7 = index(lineitem, 7)
    returned_order = Relation()
    # returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
    for ((O, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _), x1) in get(lineitem_by_7, (:r,), NONE)
        add!(returned_order, (O,), x1)
    end

    customer_nation_by_1 = index(customer_nation, 1)
    q10_customer = Relation()
    # q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
    for ((O, C, _, Date, _), x1) in orders
        Date >= 19931001 || continue
        Date < 19940101 || continue
        for x2 in probe(returned_order, (O,))
            for ((_, _), x3) in get(customer_nation_by_1, (C,), NONE)
                add!(q10_customer, (C,), x1 & x2 & x3)
            end
        end
    end

    q10 = Relation()
    # q10 :- q10_customer(_).
    for ((_,), x1) in q10_customer
        add!(q10, (), x1)
    end

    queries = (holds(q10, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

% TPC-H, tuple-independent: queries q10; the places are the files of the relations nation, customer, orders, lineitem, facts `P::relation(...)`.
:- consult($1).
:- consult($2).
:- consult($3).
:- consult($4).
q10 :- customer(C,N,_), orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_), nation(N,_,_).
query(q10).

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; tpch_q10v_500.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define nation-facts (hash-ref db "nation/3" (make-hash)))
(define customer-facts (hash-ref db "customer/3" (make-hash)))
(define orders-facts (hash-ref db "orders/5" (make-hash)))
(define lineitem-facts (hash-ref db "lineitem/13" (make-hash)))

(define customer customer-facts)

(define nation nation-facts)

(define nation-by-1 (index nation 0))
(define customer-nation (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list C N _) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref nation-by-1 (list N) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Name _) x3) t4)
      (add! customer-nation (list C Name) (&& x1 x3)))))

(define lineitem lineitem-facts)

(define orders orders-facts)

(define lineitem-by-7 (index lineitem 6))
(define returned-order (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref lineitem-by-7 (list 'r) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list O _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) x1) t2)
    (add! returned-order (list O) x1)))

(define customer-nation-by-1 (index customer-nation 0))
(define q10-customer (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs orders)])
    (match-define (cons (list O C _ Date _) x1) t2)
    (when (>= Date 19931001)
      (when (< Date 19940101)
        (for ([x3 (in-list (probe returned-order (list O)))])
          (for ([t5 (in-list (hash-ref customer-nation-by-1 (list C) null))])
            (match-define (cons (list _ _) x4) t5)
            (add! q10-customer (list C) (&& x1 x3 x4))))))))

# tpch_q10_2.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    nation_facts = get(db, "nation/3", Relation())
    customer_facts = get(db, "customer/3", Relation())
    orders_facts = get(db, "orders/5", Relation())
    lineitem_facts = get(db, "lineitem/13", Relation())

    customer = customer_facts

    lineitem = lineitem_facts

    nation = nation_facts

    orders = orders_facts

    orders_by_2 = index(orders, 2)
    lineitem_by_1_7 = index(lineitem, 1, 7)
    nation_by_1 = index(nation, 1)
    q10 = Relation()
    # q10 :- customer(C,N,_), orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_), nation(N,_,_).
    for ((C, N, _), x1) in customer
        for ((O, _, _, Date, _), x2) in get(orders_by_2, (C,), NONE)
            Date >= 19931001 || continue
            Date < 19940101 || continue
            for ((_, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _), x3) in get(lineitem_by_1_7, (O, :r), NONE)
                for ((_, _, _), x4) in get(nation_by_1, (N,), NONE)
                    add!(q10, (), x1 & x2 & x3 & x4)
                end
            end
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(q10, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; tpch_q10v_100.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define nation-facts (hash-ref db "nation/3" (make-hash)))
(define customer-facts (hash-ref db "customer/3" (make-hash)))
(define orders-facts (hash-ref db "orders/5" (make-hash)))
(define lineitem-facts (hash-ref db "lineitem/13" (make-hash)))

(define customer customer-facts)

(define nation nation-facts)

(define nation-by-1 (index nation 0))
(define customer-nation (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list C N _) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref nation-by-1 (list N) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Name _) x3) t4)
      (add! customer-nation (list C Name) (&& x1 x3)))))

(define lineitem lineitem-facts)

(define orders orders-facts)

(define lineitem-by-7 (index lineitem 6))
(define returned-order (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref lineitem-by-7 (list 'r) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list O _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) x1) t2)
    (add! returned-order (list O) x1)))

(define customer-nation-by-1 (index customer-nation 0))
(define q10-customer (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs orders)])
    (match-define (cons (list O C _ Date _) x1) t2)
    (when (>= Date 19931001)
      (when (< Date 19940101)
        (for ([x3 (in-list (probe returned-order (list O)))])
          (for ([t5 (in-list (hash-ref customer-nation-by-1 (list C) null))])
            (match-define (cons (list _ _) x4) t5)
            (add! q10-customer (list C) (&& x1 x3 x4))))))))

(define q10 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10 :- q10_customer(_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs q10-customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list _) x1) t2)
    (add! q10 (list) x1)))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds q10 (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

# tpch_q10v_50.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    nation_facts = get(db, "nation/3", Relation())
    customer_facts = get(db, "customer/3", Relation())
    orders_facts = get(db, "orders/5", Relation())
    lineitem_facts = get(db, "lineitem/13", Relation())

    customer = customer_facts

    nation = nation_facts

    nation_by_1 = index(nation, 1)
    customer_nation = Relation()
    # customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
    for ((C, N, _), x1) in customer
        for ((_, Name, _), x2) in get(nation_by_1, (N,), NONE)
            add!(customer_nation, (C, Name), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    lineitem = lineitem_facts

    orders = orders_facts

    lineitem_by_7 = index(lineitem, 7)
    returned_order = Relation()
    # returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
    for ((O, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _), x1) in get(lineitem_by_7, (:r,), NONE)
        add!(returned_order, (O,), x1)
    end

    customer_nation_by_1 = index(customer_nation, 1)
    q10_customer = Relation()
    # q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
    for ((O, C, _, Date, _), x1) in orders
        Date >= 19931001 || continue
        Date < 19940101 || continue
        for x2 in probe(returned_order, (O,))
            for ((_, _), x3) in get(customer_nation_by_1, (C,), NONE)
                add!(q10_customer, (C,), x1 & x2 & x3)
            end
        end
    end

    q10 = Relation()
    # q10 :- q10_customer(_).
    for ((_,), x1) in q10_customer
        add!(q10, (), x1)
    end

    queries = (holds(q10, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; tpch_q10_20.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define nation-facts (hash-ref db "nation/3" (make-hash)))
(define customer-facts (hash-ref db "customer/3" (make-hash)))
(define orders-facts (hash-ref db "orders/5" (make-hash)))
(define lineitem-facts (hash-ref db "lineitem/13" (make-hash)))

(define customer customer-facts)

(define lineitem lineitem-facts)

(define nation nation-facts)

(define orders orders-facts)

(define orders-by-2 (index orders 1))
(define lineitem-by-1-7 (index lineitem 0 6))
(define nation-by-1 (index nation 0))
(define q10 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10 :- customer(C,N,_), orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_), nation(N,_,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list C N _) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref orders-by-2 (list C) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list O _ _ Date _) x3) t4)
      (when (>= Date 19931001)
        (when (< Date 19940101)
          (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref lineitem-by-1-7 (list O 'r) null))])
            (match-define (cons (list _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) x5) t6)
            (for ([t8 (in-list (hash-ref nation-by-1 (list N) null))])
              (match-define (cons (list _ _ _) x7) t8)
              (add! q10 (list) (&& x1 x3 x5 x7)))))))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds q10 (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs customer)])

              (add! q10 (list) (&& x1 x3 x5 x7)))))))))

# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),

#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    nation_facts = get(db, "nation/3", Relation())
    customer_facts = get(db, "customer/3", Relation())
    orders_facts = get(db, "orders/5", Relation())
    lineitem_facts = get(db, "lineitem/13", Relation())

    customer = customer_facts

    lineitem = lineitem_facts

    nation = nation_facts

    orders = orders_facts

    orders_by_2 = index(orders, 2)
    lineitem_by_1_7 = index(lineitem, 1, 7)
    nation_by_1 = index(nation, 1)
    q10 = Relation()
    # q10 :- customer(C,N,_), orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_), nation(N,_,_).
    for ((C, N, _), x1) in customer
        for ((O, _, _, Date, _), x2) in get(orders_by_2, (C,), NONE)
            Date >= 19931001 || continue
            Date < 19940101 || continue
            for ((_, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _), x3) in get(lineitem_by_1_7, (O, :r), NONE)
                for ((_, _, _), x4) in get(nation_by_1, (N,), NONE)
                    add!(q10, (), x1 & x2 & x3 & x4)
                end
            end
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(q10, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref lineitem-by-7 (list 'r) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list O _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) x1) t2)

(define customer-nation-by-1 (index customer-nation 0))
(define q10-customer (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs orders)])
    (match-define (cons (list O C _ Date _) x1) t2)
    (when (>= Date 19931001)

            (match-define (cons (list _ _) x4) t5)
            (add! q10-customer (list C) (&& x1 x3 x4))))))))

(define q10 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10 :- q10_customer(_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs q10-customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list _) x1) t2)
    (add! q10 (list) x1)))

  (list (distribution (holds q10 (list)))))

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; tpch_q10v_50.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define nation-facts (hash-ref db "nation/3" (make-hash)))
(define customer-facts (hash-ref db "customer/3" (make-hash)))
(define orders-facts (hash-ref db "orders/5" (make-hash)))
(define lineitem-facts (hash-ref db "lineitem/13" (make-hash)))

(define customer customer-facts)

(define nation nation-facts)

(define nation-by-1 (index nation 0))
(define customer-nation (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list C N _) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref nation-by-1 (list N) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Name _) x3) t4)
      (add! customer-nation (list C Name) (&& x1 x3)))))

(define lineitem lineitem-facts)

(define orders orders-facts)

(define lineitem-by-7 (index lineitem 6))
(define returned-order (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref lineitem-by-7 (list 'r) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list O _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) x1) t2)
    (add! returned-order (list O) x1)))

(define customer-nation-by-1 (index customer-nation 0))
(define q10-customer (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs orders)])
    (match-define (cons (list O C _ Date _) x1) t2)
    (when (>= Date 19931001)
      (when (< Date 19940101)
        (for ([x3 (in-list (probe returned-order (list O)))])
          (for ([t5 (in-list (hash-ref customer-nation-by-1 (list C) null))])
            (match-define (cons (list _ _) x4) t5)
            (add! q10-customer (list C) (&& x1 x3 x4))))))))

(define q10 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10 :- q10_customer(_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs q10-customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list _) x1) t2)
    (add! q10 (list) x1)))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds q10 (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

# tpch_q10v_500.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    nation_facts = get(db, "nation/3", Relation())
    customer_facts = get(db, "customer/3", Relation())
    orders_facts = get(db, "orders/5", Relation())
    lineitem_facts = get(db, "lineitem/13", Relation())

    customer = customer_facts

    nation = nation_facts

    nation_by_1 = index(nation, 1)
    customer_nation = Relation()
    # customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
    for ((C, N, _), x1) in customer
        for ((_, Name, _), x2) in get(nation_by_1, (N,), NONE)
            add!(customer_nation, (C, Name), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    lineitem = lineitem_facts

    orders = orders_facts

    lineitem_by_7 = index(lineitem, 7)
    returned_order = Relation()
    # returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
    for ((O, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _), x1) in get(lineitem_by_7, (:r,), NONE)
        add!(returned_order, (O,), x1)
    end

    customer_nation_by_1 = index(customer_nation, 1)
    q10_customer = Relation()
    # q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
    for ((O, C, _, Date, _), x1) in orders
        Date >= 19931001 || continue
        Date < 19940101 || continue
        for x2 in probe(returned_order, (O,))
            for ((_, _), x3) in get(customer_nation_by_1, (C,), NONE)
                add!(q10_customer, (C,), x1 & x2 & x3)
            end
        end
    end

    q10 = Relation()
    # q10 :- q10_customer(_).
    for ((_,), x1) in q10_customer
        add!(q10, (), x1)
    end

    queries = (holds(q10, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; tpch_q10v_200.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define nation-facts (hash-ref db "nation/3" (make-hash)))
(define customer-facts (hash-ref db "customer/3" (make-hash)))
(define orders-facts (hash-ref db "orders/5" (make-hash)))
(define lineitem-facts (hash-ref db "lineitem/13" (make-hash)))

(define customer customer-facts)

(define nation nation-facts)

(define nation-by-1 (index nation 0))
(define customer-nation (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list C N _) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref nation-by-1 (list N) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ Name _) x3) t4)
      (add! customer-nation (list C Name) (&& x1 x3)))))

(define lineitem lineitem-facts)

(define orders orders-facts)

(define lineitem-by-7 (index lineitem 6))
(define returned-order (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref lineitem-by-7 (list 'r) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list O _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) x1) t2)
    (add! returned-order (list O) x1)))

(define customer-nation-by-1 (index customer-nation 0))
(define q10-customer (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs orders)])
    (match-define (cons (list O C _ Date _) x1) t2)
    (when (>= Date 19931001)
      (when (< Date 19940101)
        (for ([x3 (in-list (probe returned-order (list O)))])
          (for ([t5 (in-list (hash-ref customer-nation-by-1 (list C) null))])
            (match-define (cons (list _ _) x4) t5)
            (add! q10-customer (list C) (&& x1 x3 x4))))))))

(define q10 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; q10 :- q10_customer(_).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs q10-customer)])
    (match-define (cons (list _) x1) t2)
    (add! q10 (list) x1)))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds q10 (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

# tpch_q10v_5.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    nation_facts = get(db, "nation/3", Relation())
    customer_facts = get(db, "customer/3", Relation())
    orders_facts = get(db, "orders/5", Relation())
    lineitem_facts = get(db, "lineitem/13", Relation())

    customer = customer_facts

    nation = nation_facts

    nation_by_1 = index(nation, 1)
    customer_nation = Relation()
    # customer_nation(C,Name) :- customer(C,N,_), nation(N,Name,_).
    for ((C, N, _), x1) in customer
        for ((_, Name, _), x2) in get(nation_by_1, (N,), NONE)
            add!(customer_nation, (C, Name), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    lineitem = lineitem_facts

    orders = orders_facts

    lineitem_by_7 = index(lineitem, 7)
    returned_order = Relation()
    # returned_order(O) :- lineitem(O,_,_,_,_,_,r,_,_,_,_,_,_).
    for ((O, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _), x1) in get(lineitem_by_7, (:r,), NONE)
        add!(returned_order, (O,), x1)
    end

    customer_nation_by_1 = index(customer_nation, 1)
    q10_customer = Relation()
    # q10_customer(C) :- orders(O,C,_,Date,_), Date >= 19931001, Date < 19940101, returned_order(O), customer_nation(C,_).
    for ((O, C, _, Date, _), x1) in orders
        Date >= 19931001 || continue
        Date < 19940101 || continue
        for x2 in probe(returned_order, (O,))
            for ((_, _), x3) in get(customer_nation_by_1, (C,), NONE)
                add!(q10_customer, (C,), x1 & x2 & x3)
            end
        end
    end

    q10 = Relation()
    # q10 :- q10_customer(_).
    for ((_,), x1) in q10_customer
        add!(q10, (), x1)
    end

    queries = (holds(q10, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end
